LESSON: EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATION BY THE END OF THE SUB-STRAND, LISTENING

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: What makes us LISTENING the learner should be able to: feelings (texts on health and hygiene), happy?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. practise Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING
2. use Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING in clear sentences

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING

Teach
• Focus skill: Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What makes us LISTENING the learner should be able to: feelings (texts on health and hygiene), happy?
2. What makes us sad?
3. How do we respond communication to express audio-visual teaching aids to relate to when someone is sad?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
